review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, and a second production run of cs_app::roster::survey_retail_neutral_traffic over the installation (neutral-traffic-census.json). Claim is implemented only. The census measures one observable of the original installation: per mission directory ZBD/<group>/<mission>, whether its own reader archive ZBD/<group>/<mission>/zrdr.zbd carries the member named zeppelins.zrd, and whether any installation-scope archive (ZBD/zrdr.zbd or ZBD/<group>/zrdr.zbd) does. LIMITS OF WHAT WAS MEASURED, each outside F33-D's census scope and recorded in docs/findings/2026-10-03-f33-d-neutral-traffic-population-and-retail-census.md: (1) the member name zeppelins.zrd is a name rule inferred from the mission archives; its role and its encoding are NOT decoded, so this census does not show that the game used it for neutral traffic or how an actor is encoded in it; (2) no mapping from a runtime ActorId to any original script/actor id exists; (3) whether the original spawns any neutral traffic at all, and how it treats an omitted author list, is unknown: no original executable was run, and reading the installation's files is not evidence of how the game behaves; (4) the original's cutscene death, voice and ally-loss behavior is unmeasured. The population seam itself is exercised by the unignored acceptance tests over authored synthetic fixtures; the three mission omissions are a measured fact of the installation, not a claim about runtime behavior. `unknowns` is empty because the measurement itself has nothing unresolved; every mission directory resolved to an archive with a measured SHA-256 and member count. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass.
